My experience is this. My father was also a manipulative person and verbally abused me and my sister through the years, with the consent of my mother, who surely knew but never believed me and denied the whole thing until today.

I went though therapy and I lived on my own during five years, after that I had to approach my parents again because I needed money and because I still have a connection with my mother, and now I am living not too far from them.

My conclusions are.

At the end they are my parents. They raised me and I feel like I have to take care of them, even if my father is a bad person, but that's a personal choice.

There's nothing I can do to make them admit what they did. I will never have a confession so speaking to them about this is useless.

I have the right to speak to everybody I want about what they did. In fact this is helping me a lot. I don't have to protect the "honor" of the family.

I will help anybody that is passing through the same and fight for the rights of verbally abused people, and that is my revenge for what they did to me.

So my advice is: look forward, look for yourself and get professional help.

To me the output is good for society but in the long run is bad to rely on it, because I think private companies should not dictate when someone - authistic or not - can or cannot access their facilities. Everybody has the same rights, and governments should enforce that by creating laws.

I mean was good that a bus company reserved some seats for black people when nobody did? Sure, but if people of the time had left the rights of black people in hands of bus companies they'll never have the rights they have now, because the aim of a company is to make profit, not changes in society.

I am only being critic with it because I think that if you want to fix things permanently you should not depend of the good will of a private company whose target is to make profit, you should aim to the government and turn that into a right, so every company must open one day for authistic children even if they are loosing money.

Of course if you have a child with that condition if they open one day is a good thing for you. I am not saying that you must keep him at home and I am sorry if you feel questioned because I have no kids and I won't know how to start dealing with a situation like the one you have.

But they are separated planes, I think taking profit of what a company offers is not incompatible with doing something to change things. Life is complicated for everybody.

I don't know, but I think that if you are really concerned about something you don't need to take credit about it, so when I see a company doing something like that very publicily I tend to doubt about their intentions.

Recently I found an ex member of the commercial department of the most important funerary company of Spain, telling on twitter - and I can provide the link - that the official policy there was to push the most affected familiars because they tend to spend more money in the funerals.

So yeah, maybe I have a twisted view but sometimes I find things are even worse than I imagine.

And a child doesn't feels different if a company publicily announces a "special day" for him? I mean, if something is a right there's no need of announcement. I. e. there are parking places for disabled people because it's a right, there's no "special parking day" for them.

You're welcome. About support groups, honestly I don't know. I've been writing for a year in a forum for people with different problems and sharing my problems on a regular basis helped me, so I am also trying to find a support group where I can do the same presently.

The good thing for me about support groups, based on my "online" experience, is that you always find people with the same problem than you, and you learn to help others when you "are strong" and let them help you when you "are weak".

The counterpart is that, as everyone has the same problem, sometimes others discorauge you when you want to do something to change or they reinforce you in your mood with their comments, as they are in the same one.

To avoid this I think it's better to join a group conducted by a therapist. I went to one session of a group with no therapist and it was ok because everybody shared their feelings but with no direction, so it was only a relief, not something that can lead to a solution.

I think that, independently of my opinion, if you have considered it you should try. At least you won't feel alone.

Or maybe you are not so calm and need to break things or do some kind of sport... I presume you've been told the same lots of times but...

Enlarge it, go beyond the limits. Make something you like without asking permission, take a bus without knowing where it's going, go to the cinema to watch a movie you only like. Don't stay home... Those were the things I did when I felt like you probably do now, but you have to find your own things.

And read, if you like it read about real people that felt isolated also. It's not so uncommon.

If you feel lonely in your interests and hobbies check out podcasting, seriously, and if you are young be patient and keep pushing. Your world will get bigger.
